decision.top3_series_pattern: trend-dominated, high predictability, moderate seasonality, non‑stationary, robust combination recommended
decision.top3_why: Candidate A achieves the lowest validation score (0.6557) and shows the most stable performance across the three validation windows (0.6909, 0.6569, 0.6262). Its weights are derived from a gradient‑boosted model trained on all other series in a leave‑one‑series‑out fashion, providing a data‑driven yet generalizable weighting scheme that is less likely to overfit to the idiosyncrasies of this single series. The diagnosis flags unstable model ranking and correlated errors, so a robust weighted combination is preferred, which A delivers.
decision.top3_why_not: Candidates B and C use inverse‑error weighting on the full pool, yielding higher validation scores (0.6664) and more volatile per‑window performance (especially the third window, 0.7181 and 0.7256). Their reliance on error estimates, which are noisy with only three validation windows, makes them more susceptible to overfitting and less robust in the presence of unstable rankings and correlated errors. Therefore, they are less suitable than A for generalization to the blind test window.
decision.justification: Candidate A achieves the lowest validation score (0.6557) and shows the most stable performance across the three validation windows (0.6909, 0.6569, 0.6262).
